publisher: Department of Justice Canada (Justice Laws Website) - Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, SOR/2002-227, section 300
research_notes: Taken from the regulation itself rather than the IRCC fee list, because canada.ca repeatedly returned HTTP 404 on fee-related paths during this session while the Justice Laws consolidation served the same figure and is the statutory authority. The marginal note reads exactly 'Fee — $150' and subsection 300(1) reads 'A fee of $150 is payable for processing an application for a study permit.' Currency is CAD. IMPORTANT CONTEXT THAT THE $150 FIGURE CONCEALS: this is a PROCESSING fee only. A study permit applicant in the ordinary course also pays for the initial passport, medicals and police certificates, plus any provincial document requirement, and - as recorded in 002_financial_proof.json - must show funds for tuition, living expenses and transportation. So $150 is not the cost of getting a Canadian study visa. NO HEALTH SURCHARGE ANALOGUE: unlike the UK (Immigration Health Surcharge, recorded at GB/003b), the fee schedule for a Canadian study permit contains no per-year health component, and I did not find one; I have NOT asserted that none exists in every circumstance, only that section 300 sets out a single flat processing fee with the exemptions listed. The nine fee exemptions in subsection 300(2) are recorded verbatim and are broader than most applicants expect: pending and accepted refugee claimants, Convention Refugee and Humanitarian-Assisted Person classes abroad, diplomats and their suites, visiting forces and civilian components, temporarily destitute current permit holders, students under bilateral reciprocal exchange agreements, certain US pre-inspection staff, and certain US officials on temporary posting. Clause (g) is the one most relevant to scholarship applicants: study under a Canada-country agreement providing for reciprocity of student exchange is fee-exempt. CITATION NOTE: the amendments credited to this section are SOR/2011-222 s.9, SOR/2014-19 s.5 and SOR/2015-25 s.5(E) - i.e. the $150 figure itself has not been amended in the versions displayed, though the regulations as a whole were last amended 2026-07-15. NOT VERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: the 'Restore your status as a student' composite fee of CAD 396.25 and the CAD 246.25 status-restoration fee, which appeared only in IRCC search-engine snippets (ircc.canada.ca fee list, dated 2026-09-21) that I did not fetch; biometrics fees; and the Canadian eTA / TRV costs. Those are excluded rather than asserted.

claims.statement: A fee of CAD 150 is payable for processing an application for a Canadian study permit.

The CAD 150 study permit fee is a processing fee only and is not the total cost of obtaining a Canadian study visa; no per-year health surcharge is set under section 300 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations.

The study permit processing fee is waived for nine classes of person, including students whose study in Canada is under an agreement or arrangement between Canada and another country providing for reciprocity of student exchange programs.
